tldr: This is a loose theme thread, not one event: three unrelated sources over two weeks treated the inference engine itself as the object of work. It opened with EngineAgent, a paper on using agents to port new LLM architectures into on-device engines, and a Nov 22 paper on stripping backdoor activations at inference time.
whats_new: Humanity's Last System (HLS), an open benchmark, gives coding agents live GPU sandboxes for up to 36 hours to build inference servers that are verified and scored for speed against vLLM-style baselines.
why_it_matters: Agent-written serving code is moving from research prototype to scored benchmark, so the speed claims around custom inference engines will soon come with a public yardstick against vLLM.

beats.headline: EngineAgent proposes agents that adapt on-device engines to new LLM architectures
beats.summary: Frames per-model engine support across heterogeneous mobile hardware as recurring, costly work worth automating.

beats.headline: Training-free SVD filter cuts backdoor attack success to about 2% at inference
beats.summary: A security result on CNN and ViT models; it shares the inference-time framing, not the agent theme.

beats.headline: HLS benchmark asks whether agents can build an inference server that beats vLLM

open_questions: Does any agent-built server in HLS beat the vLLM baseline on published results?
Which models and GPUs does HLS score on, and does the verification step check output correctness as well as speed?
Does EngineAgent release code or results for a named on-device engine?
take_for_builders: Treat agent-built inference servers as unproven until HLS publishes verified scores; keep vLLM as the serving baseline and rerun your own latency evals before swapping engines.

day_captions.f9d81d0a259ab7bb: First framing of engine porting as an agent task, scoped to on-device inference.
day_captions.9aba4bf153849718: Adds an inference-time defense angle: backdoor success averaged 2.07% across five models.
day_captions.781ec9697da4f86b: Turns agent-built engines into an open, scored benchmark with vLLM-style baselines.
